title: Guided evening
description: One guided evening (a walk through the sky, step by step). A written evening lists its steps, one list per hemisphere and season; a computed evening holds only the rules and the wrapping texts, and the app computes its steps from the place, the date and the horizon. Every text is in texts/<locale>.json under a key derived from this file: <id>.title, <id>.subtitle, <id>.intro, <id>.outro, <id>.title.<season> (written), <id>.<list>.subtitle and <id>.<list>.<step> (written), <id>.<text> (computed). French is the source of meaning. tests/guided-evenings.test.mjs checks the references, the visibility of every written list and the length of every text.

id.description: Stable identifier, also the file name and the prefix of the text keys.

sheetOrder.description: Position of the evening's card in the choice sheet (1 = first).

kind.description: written: the steps are the lists below; computed: the app computes them (see computed).

level.description: beginner: nothing to know beforehand; curious: some patience to find faint shapes; telescope: a telescope and its handling.

observingModes.description: The ways of observing the evening goes with, as the first step of the choice sheet offers them: naked (the eyes alone), binoculars (held in the hand), tripod (binoculars or a telescope on a tripod, the phone on it for the pointing aid), mount (a GoTo mount, refined by the phone), smartTelescope (a smart telescope points and stacks by itself). The person chooses the way; the pointing aid is their choice too, never the evening's.

estimatedMinutes.description: Typical length of the evening, for the card (a written list may say its own).

seasons.description: Astronomical seasons of the place's own hemisphere (southern spring runs from the September equinox to the December solstice).

lists.description: Written evenings: one list per hemisphere and season.

id.description: <hemisphere>-<season>; the prefix of the list's text keys.

step.description: One step. Its text (<evening>.<list>.<step>) says where to look from the step before, what one sees and one thing to know, in two to four sentences; it completes the target's own sheet and never repeats it.

type.description: brightStar: one of the 92 bright stars (target hip:<HIP>); constellation: one of the 88 (target = IAU abbreviation); deepSky: a catalogue object (target = catalogue id); solarSystem: the Moon or a planet (target = catalogue id); lookAround: no target, the sky itself (anchor = where the map opens).

target.description: hip:<HIP> (brightStar), the IAU abbreviation (constellation), the catalogue id of the target index (deepSky: openngc-…, solarSystem: solar-system-…).

designation.description: deepSky only: the designation of the catalogue row (M42, NGC 2392), for the reader of this file; checked against the catalogue.

anchor.description: lookAround only: the constellation (IAU abbreviation) the map opens on.

computed.description: The rules of a computed evening. The app takes the candidates of source above minAltitudeDegrees (and above the horizon mask) during the first hours of darkness, keeps the count brightest, and orders them; it hides the evening when nothing is left and hideWhenEmpty is true. A step's text is one lead text (optional) followed by one body text (required): for each slot, the first text of texts, in this order, whose conditions all hold.

source.description: brightStars: the 92 bright stars of sky-data/bright-stars.json; solarSystem: the bodies listed.

count.description: At most this many steps (none: every candidate).

order.description: westToEast: by hour angle, the step furthest west (the first to set) first.

genericText.description: A text of a computed step; its key is <evening>.<id>. A lead text is one sentence, a body text two or three.

when.description: Every condition must hold; an empty object always holds.

altitudeBelowDegrees.description: The target's altitude when the step opens.

waxing.description: The Moon: true from new to full Moon.
